bacteria: Bacteria seen under a microscope, rod-shaped and round cells crowding the whole field of view
barley: Ears of barley standing shoulder to shoulder across the whole frame, long bristles rising from every head
capsule: A bottle neck filling the frame with a dark foil capsule sleeved over its cork, the cut edge of the foil showing across the middle
cork: Bottle corks packed tightly together and running off every edge, their speckled bark surface filling the frame
grain: A mass of barley grains filling the whole frame, each an oval with a crease down the middle
grist: Coarsely milled malt filling the frame, pale flour shot through with darker shards of broken husk
malt: Sprouted barley kernels packed across the frame, each one with a short pale rootlet pushing out of its tip
mash: The surface of hot mash filling the frame, a thick porridge of ground malt and water with a wooden paddle resting in it and steam lifting off
prong: The four tines of a table fork cropped very close, each separate point running up out of the frame
rake: The head of a rake cropped close, its steel bar spanning the frame and a long row of curved teeth raking down out of view
sprout: A split seed shown very large, a thick white root driving down into dark soil and a green shoot pushing up out of the frame
starch: A potato cut in half and filling the frame, its brown skin around the rim and the pale cut flesh dense with white starch granules
suture: A closed wound filling the frame, its two edges drawn together by a row of evenly spaced stitches with knotted thread ends
washback: Looking down into a wooden washback, the fermenting liquid filling it with a thick head of froth right to the staves
wort: Sweet amber wort filling the frame to the brim of its vessel, a pale head of foam across the top and bubbles rising through the liquid
yeast: Yeast cells crowding the frame, round and cream coloured, several with a smaller bud growing off one side
